title: Elysia cookie session login
context: Cookie login backed by a server-side `sessions` store (get/set(id, data, ttlSeconds)/del). The session id must be freshly generated at every login. The cookie must be httpOnly, secure, sameSite lax and expire together with the 8-hour session. Logout must destroy the server-side session.
code: export const auth = new Elysia({ name: "auth" })
await sessions.set(id, { user: { id: user.id, role: user.role } }, EIGHT_HOURS);
sid.set({ value: id, httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax", maxAge: EIGHT_HOURS * 1000, path: "/" });
}, { body: t.Object({ email: t.String(), password: t.String() }) })
if (!user) { set.status = 401; return { error: "not logged in" }; }

expected.why: reuses a pre-existing session id (session fixation); a new id must be issued on every login
cookie maxAge is in seconds; * 1000 makes the cookie last about 11 months instead of 8 hours
only the cookie is cleared; the server-side session is never deleted, so a stolen sid keeps working
